This is the absolute LAST post I ever expected to be making on the Monday of my bodybuilding show week.

After months of weighing every gram of food, tracking every calorie, hitting my workouts, doing my cardio, practicing my posing, and preparing myself mentally, physically, and spiritually to step on stage this Saturday, I spent this past weekend binge eating in a way I’ve never experienced before.

And when I say binge eating, I don’t mean I went out and enjoyed a cheat meal or ate a little more than I was supposed to.

I mean I completely lost control.

I kept eating long after my stomach was telling me to stop. I was physically uncomfortable, I wasn’t even enjoying the food anymore, and yet I continued eating.

And the scariest part wasn’t even the amount of food I consumed.

It was what was going through my head while I was doing it.

At a certain point, it felt like I was intentionally sabotaging myself. Like there was a part of me that wanted to ruin everything I had worked so hard for.

And I’ve spent the last couple of days asking myself WHY.

Was I afraid I wasn’t going to look good enough on stage? Was I afraid of disappointing myself? Was I putting so much pressure on myself that I subconsciously wanted a way out?

I don’t have all the answers.

But those are some uncomfortable questions I’ve had to start asking myself.

After the first binge, I told my coach Chris Elkins everything. Every single thing I ate. We talked about it, and the plan was to move forward, reassess, and take things day by day.

The next day, I got right back to my routine. Tracked my food, followed my plan, and genuinely thought I had moved past what happened.

Then nighttime came.

What started as one extra bite of food turned into another binge. And this one was even worse than the first.

I can’t even explain how disappointed I felt afterward.

Not because I had eaten food that wasn’t on my plan. But because I had reached a point where I felt like I couldn’t stop myself from doing something I knew was hurting me.

I woke up physically miserable. My face was extremely swollen, my body felt awful, and I was looking at myself in the mirror trying to understand how I had gotten here.

And now here I am.

Five days away from the competition I’ve spent months preparing for, roughly 10 pounds heavier than I was going into the weekend, and genuinely uncertain whether I’m going to step on stage this Saturday.

Chris believes competing is still an option. Part of me wants to finish what I started. Another part of me wonders whether postponing until November would be the better decision.

Because I know how much work I put into this prep. And I also know that the choices I made this weekend have consequences.

I’m not going to sit here and blame anybody else. I’m not going to pretend it didn’t happen. And I’m definitely not going to ask anyone to feel sorry for me.

But I also don’t want to spend the rest of my life beating myself up over two days.

I made those choices. I have to own them. And now I have to figure out how to move forward.

One thing this weekend has forced me to recognize is just how much pressure I’ve been putting on myself. Not only with bodybuilding, but with life in general.

Constantly working. Constantly thinking about what’s next. Constantly being on my phone. Constantly feeling like I need to be doing MORE.

And somewhere along the way, I stopped giving myself enough room to just live.

So regardless of whether I compete Saturday or in November, some things are going to change.

I’m prioritizing my sleep. I’m taking real breaks from social media. I’m giving myself time to recover. And I’m going to take a serious look at my relationship with food and the pressure I’ve been putting on myself.

I’m not going to pretend I’ve figured everything out in 48 hours. I haven’t.

And I don’t want to turn this into some inspirational story about how I fell down and immediately got back up stronger than ever.

I’m still figuring it out.

NEW: Florida police release a statement after a family claims that police were called on their 3-year-old son because he was "too good" at soccer.

Video footage shows a 3-year-old soccer prodigy dominating a group of 5-year-olds in Winter Park, Florida.

"They called the police on a three-year-old because he's too good... because he had the ball for too long and nobody else can get the ball so they called the police on him," the family claimed in the video.

The Winter Park Police Department has since released a statement saying they were called about a "disturbance" between league officials and the player's parents.

"The Winter Park Police Department was contacted by a soccer league official who requested response to a disturbance between league officials and the parents of a player," they said.

"The league requested the family leave and offered to refund the league cost to family. Shortly after arrival, the officers were requested by the league official to communicate with the family as he did not want to further a disturbance."

"The family stated the game was over and they were leaving. The family was cooperative with the officers and were provided with an event number for the incident at their request."

"The incident was a civil matter between those parties and not criminal. No one was arrested, trespassed, or forced to leave the park. The Officers body worn cameras confirm the above information."

X ALGORITHM UPDATE 🚨

X just stopped cutting new posts first, and that should help small accounts (I check it daily with Claude and share updates worth sharing with you)

tl;dr:

- X can only check 2,800 posts each time you open your feed
- new posts used to be last in line, so they got cut first
- now everything gets cut equally, new posts included
- posts labeled low quality or misinfo now show a warning, and people can't like, reply or share them
- no score changes this time

lesson learned: your new posts now get a fair chance to be seen. Your first 2 hours still matter most.

full details:

- How it worked until this week

Every time someone opens For You, X collects around 3,700 posts it could show them: posts from people they follow, popular posts, posts liked by similar people, and brand new posts.

But X only has time to check 2,800 of them.

So it just took the first 2,800 in line. Brand new posts were at the back of the line. When there were too many, they were the ones left out... and a post that never gets checked can't be shown.

- What changed

Now everything gets cut by the same amount. 25% too many? Every type of post loses 25%, new posts included. Nobody goes first.

- Why small accounts should care

Those brand new posts are under 2 hours old, with under 8 likes and under 500 views. That's where most posts from smaller accounts are.

My read: they now get a fair chance instead of being cut first. How often X actually hits the 2,800 limit isn't in the code, so I can't tell you how big the difference is.

- Low quality and misinfo posts now show a warning

If X labels your post as low quality or misinformation, people who don't follow you see a warning on it, and they can't like, reply, repost, bookmark or share it. The code doesn't say what gets a post that label.

Here's a recap of what you should be doing:

- a new post gets its extra push only in its first 2 hours and first 200 views, so post when your people are online
- likes carry more weight than ever at 0.66 each
- people sticking around pays, the time-spent score is 50% higher than two weeks ago
- a read of 10+ seconds after someone opens your post adds 0.4
- the boost favors the post with the best like rate from its first viewers
- accounts up to 50K can get one fresh original lifted to roughly 16th
- nothing beats a copy link share, it scores 20
- replies, quotes and DM shares each score 5
- talk with your mutuals, replies between you score 20 instead of 5
- originals are the only posts that travel outside your follower base
- the 1st and the 32nd like each open a new route to strangers
- your 2nd post in the same feed is worth 62% of the first, so pick your best one
- videos still need 10+ seconds to qualify for the video lists
- earning a follow adds 4
- a pinned post with a bad link can flag the account for 7 days, worth a quick check

What you should NOT be doing:

- posts that get labeled low quality or misinfo now carry a warning, and nobody outside your followers can like or share them
- video alone won't carry you, an open counts 0.02 and the watch 0
- hide-worthy posts cost more, "not interested" sits at -52.27
- a post at 3am burns its 2 hour window before anyone sees it
- a tap that turns into a bounce is worth only 0.3
- replies and reposts don't get past your followers
- insults get your post hidden from anyone who doesn't follow you
- adult media in 3 of your last 5 posts puts a label on your account
- disguised content in videos gets checked from 64 likes, harder at 512
- self-reply chains under big accounts risk being zeroed
- one account label and non-followers stop seeing you entirely
- low-rated links don't belong in your pinned post
- recycled wording can get tagged as copypasta spam
- strangers tagged plus a low quality link is a pattern X flags
- engagement bait has no size exemption
- several posts in a row end up competing with each other
- hashtag stacks add nothing
- bookmarks are still worth 0
- 48 hours in, For You is finished with a post

SEAL Team 7 Alpha Platoon in Heavy Combat — Battle of Mosul (2017)

Footage from 2017 shows operators from SEAL Team 7’s Alpha Platoon on the front lines during the brutal Battle of Mosul. The video captures the raw intensity and precision of U.S. Navy SEALs fighting house-to-house in one of the toughest urban battles of the modern era.

Operators engage in intense close-quarters combat as they help liberate the city from ISIS.
